beats.text: Five Stoic lessons on building real self-discipline.
One. Do what must be done, not what you feel like. Feelings are weather; duty is the compass.
Two. Discipline is freedom. Every craving you can refuse is a chain you're choosing not to wear.
Three. Train in good times for the hard ones. Comfort practised becomes weakness under pressure.
Four. Master the small things — the snooze button, the extra scroll. Big discipline is many tiny ones.
Five. You will not always be motivated. You can always be committed. Commitment is what remains.
The Stoic doesn't wait to feel ready. He acts on principle — and lets the feeling catch up.
